summary: Rakoty is a small East Brunswick accounting firm built around nonprofit clients: bookkeeping, grant and budget reporting, audit leadership, 990 preparation and payroll, plus a sideline in small-business bookkeeping and tax. It presents itself as a team with 70+ years of combined experience and displays roughly two dozen nonprofit client logos, several of them national or out-of-state. Its web front door is effectively broken: every page stalls behind a percentage preloader, the 'Schedule an appointment' buttons have no working link, and there is no form, scheduler or chat anywhere on the site.

facts.fact: Office at 82 Brunswick Woods Dr, East Brunswick, NJ 08816; phone (732) 338-8807; email info@RakotyGroup.com; hours stated as Mon-Fri 9am-5pm in the site header (the footer of the same pages says 'Visit Us Daily').

Nonprofit service list published on the home page: accounting and bookkeeping, budgeting and reporting, audit and 990 reports, training and support, government grants management, full payroll, customized services, technical support.
A dedicated landing page advertises bookkeeping at a published $99/month, alongside 'over 70 years of combined experience'.

Nonprofit page promises a 'dedicated Client Manager' acting as part-time CFO or full-time bookkeeper, monthly close by the 10th, grant budget-to-actual tracking, W-2/1099/1096 preparation, payroll 'on biweekly basis and perform basic HR services', and offers managed IT services.
Home page displays about 24 client logos including NRCDV, JCCA, Agora University, Sudanese American Physicians Association, Wafa House, Coptic Cross Ministries and Sunshine Pharmacy.

Google Business Profile is named 'Rakoty Accountants', categorised 'Accounting firm', located in Brunswick Woods Office Park, and showed 5.0 stars from 16 reviews as of 8 Nov 2026 (per a third-party directory quoting Google).
Google Maps listing shows 5.0 stars, address 82 Brunswick Woods Dr, phone (732) 338-8807, website link, 'Closed - Opens 9 AM Mon'; the limited Maps view did not display a review count.

Every page stalls on a full-screen percentage preloader: at 1440px the taxes page sat at 9%, the home page at 32% at 500px width, and the contacts page climbed from 12% to 27% at 390px width with no page content rendered.

The hero 'Schedule an appointment' button links to https://rakotygroup.com/contacts-us/, which returns HTTP 404; the nav and in-page 'Schedule an appointment' buttons have no href at all. /careers/ also returns 404.
The contacts page has no contact form: the only form element on the site is the header site-search box, though Contact Form 7 and WPForms plugins are loaded.

The /about-rakoty/ page still carries unedited theme demo copy ('Make Digital Marketing Work For Your Business') with fictitious staff ('Monica Black, chief communication officer', 'Peter Adams, co-founder of company'); /non-profit/ likewise shows template consulting copy referencing 'Radar Strategy'.

Page title is 'Rakoty - Nonprofit Accounting company' (no town, no 'East Brunswick'), the meta description mixes real text with placeholder phrasing ('Accounting Company or a natural variation like accounting firm with a focus on nonprofits'), and the Yoast JSON-LD graph is WebPage/Organization with no LocalBusiness/AccountingService, address or phone.

Site runs WordPress with Elementor (stylesheet v3.23.0, Aug 2024) and Yoast SEO v28.1, loads Google Tag Manager container GTM-W5QWST8X, links Facebook, LinkedIn and Instagram, and carries no booking, chat or CRM widget in the markup.

Page sitemap shows pages re-edited in Aug-Oct 2026 (bookkeeping offer 2026-08-28, contacts 2026-09-15, non-profit-2 2026-10-12) and a blog last posted 2025-09-18; a Google Ads creative ('Google-ads-Desktop-contact') was uploaded 2026-10.

Third-party org directory lists Rakoty Nonprofit Consultants at 11-50 employees and describes it as providing affordable financial and technical management, including leading the annual audit and 990 preparation.

A Google review displayed on a directory page praises a 'seamless transition to QuickBooks' plus ongoing day-to-day finance support for a nationwide nonprofit; another credits the firm with helping 'catch up to billings' for an NYC foster-care nonprofit.

operations_signals: Lead intake runs on phone, email and walk-in only: 'Call Us (732) 338-8807' and 'Mail Us info@RakotyGroup.com' on a page with no form, no calendar and no chat (https://rakotygroup.com/contacts/).

The advertised booking path is broken: hero and nav 'Schedule an appointment' CTAs point to a 404 (/contacts-us/) or have no href, so a would-be nonprofit client cannot request a consultation online (https://rakotygroup.com/).
Stated hours Mon-Fri 9am-5pm from the header, but the footer on the same pages says 'Visit Us Daily' - two conflicting statements on every page (https://rakotygroup.com/contacts/).

Engagement model is a named 'Client Manager' serving as part-time CFO or full-time bookkeeper, with monthly close targeted for the 10th and weekly vendor payment runs after approvals (https://rakotygroup.com/non-profit-2/).

Deliverables are document-heavy and recurring: annual audit leadership, 990 filing, grant budget-to-actual by month and quarter, cost allocation across grants, 1099/W-2 season (https://rakotygroup.com/non-profit-2/).

Clients appear to be remote/multi-state (Philadelphia nonprofit, NYC foster-care nonprofit, 'we serve small organizations all over the nation'), so most coordination is not in-person (https://rakotygroup.com/small-businesses/).
hiring_signals: No careers page exists on the site (/careers/ returns HTTP 404); no job postings were found on Indeed, ZipRecruiter, Glassdoor or LinkedIn in searches run 2026-11-13 (https://rakotygroup.com/).
Directory listings put the firm at 11-50 employees, which implies a bookkeeping/payroll/preparer bench but no verified open roles (https://theorg.com/org/rakoty-nonprofit-consultants).
review_themes: All five Google reviews visible on a directory mirror are 5-star and dated roughly 4-8 months ago; consistent praise for responsiveness, nonprofit expertise and grants/compliance knowledge (https://www.dosfinds.us/firms/rakoty-accountants).

Repeated theme: rescuing backlogged books and billing - one client credits them with helping 'catch up to billings' and hitting deadlines, another with a smooth QuickBooks migration (https://www.dosfinds.us/firms/rakoty-accountants).
Longevity theme: one client testimonial says Rakoty has been their 'one-stop-shop' since 2018 (https://rakotygroup.com/non-profit-2/).

No negative review themes surfaced in any source checked; no Yelp or BBB listing was found, so the sample is essentially the firm's own testimonials plus ~16 Google reviews (https://taxscout.ai/cpa/rakoty-llc-e-brunswick-nj).
tech_footprint: WordPress + Elementor (v3.23.0, Aug 2024 build) with Yoast SEO v28.1; theme Maxbizz plus a 'Royal Preloader' splash that never completes (https://rakotygroup.com/).
No scheduling, chat, client portal or CRM tool in the markup; Contact Form 7 and WPForms plugins are installed but zero forms render (https://rakotygroup.com/contacts/).
Google Tag Manager (GTM-W5QWST8X) is installed; there is no Google Analytics snippet and no consent banner, so measurement depends entirely on GTM (https://rakotygroup.com/).

Published content: an active blog with IRS 990, cost-allocation, accrual-basis and partnership-tax articles through Sept 2025, plus a $99/month bookkeeping offer landing page (https://rakotygroup.com/blog/).
Social presence linked from every page: Facebook (/Nonprofits.Accountants), LinkedIn (/company/rakoty) and Instagram; LinkedIn was not readable (HTTP 403) in this session (https://rakotygroup.com/).
growth_signals: Pages were substantially rewritten in Aug-Oct 2026 (bookkeeping offer, nonprofit page, contacts) and a Google Ads desktop creative was uploaded in Oct 2026, suggesting active paid-marketing investment this year (https://rakotygroup.com/page-sitemap.xml).

A published $99/month bookkeeping product is aimed at volume acquisition rather than bespoke CFO work, a shift toward productised, lower-touch revenue (https://rakotygroup.com/bookkeeping-services-offer/).

Client roster has grown to roughly two dozen nonprofit logos including national bodies (NRCDV, JCCA, Neurosurgical Society of the Virginias) and out-of-state clients, implying multi-state service delivery (https://rakotygroup.com/).
Service line has expanded beyond accounting to managed IT (email, networking, cloud, security), payroll/HR and QuickBooks implementation (https://rakotygroup.com/non-profit-2/).
Copy references bringing in new talent and acquiring companies, but that text sits on an unedited theme demo page and was not verified elsewhere (https://rakotygroup.com/about-rakoty/).
physical_signals: Single office at 82 Brunswick Woods Dr, East Brunswick, NJ 08816, inside Brunswick Woods Office Park per Google Maps; no square footage, seat count or headcount published (https://www.google.com/maps/search/Rakoty+Nonprofit+Accountants+82+Brunswick+Woods+Dr+East+Brunswick+NJ).
Physical footprint is a professional office suite, not a retail counter: address appears in the header, footer and a Google map embed on the contacts page (https://rakotygroup.com/contacts/).
No fleet, kitchen, warehouse or equipment inventory is advertised; service delivery is remote or onsite at client locations ('Maintain your Books remotely or onsite') (https://rakotygroup.com/).
No public health-inspection, OSHA, FMCSA or permit records are applicable or were found for an accounting office of this type (https://taxscout.ai/cpa/rakoty-llc-e-brunswick-nj).
decision_maker: Unknown - the firm's own site names no owner, partner or staff member. Client testimonials on the site and in Google reviews repeatedly address the principal only as 'Bass' (e.g. 'Every meeting with Bass'); a third-party tax directory titles its Rakoty LLC profile 'Bassem Massoud' without stating a title (https://taxscout.ai/cpa/rakoty-llc-e-brunswick-nj).

inferences.inference: Inbound leads are being lost at the front door, and mobile visitors are the worst hit.
inferences.reasoning: Every page I loaded (home, taxes, contacts) hung on a percentage preloader with no content, at both 1440px and 390px; the only real call path is a phone number that a visitor cannot see. The CTA that would normally capture demand ('Schedule an appointment') is a dead link or no link at all.

inferences.inference: Marketing spend is running against a site that cannot convert.
inferences.reasoning: New landing pages and a Google Ads creative were added Aug-Oct 2026 and GTM is installed, so there is budget and intent to generate demand, but the rendered site is blank and there is no form - paid clicks have nowhere to land.

inferences.inference: The firm's biggest manual load is document chasing and deadline tracking across grant and audit cycles.
inferences.reasoning: The published scope includes monthly closes by the 10th, grant budget-to-actual reporting monthly and quarterly, annual audit leadership with state auditors (per the Rising Hope testimonial), 990 filings and year-end 1099/W-2 runs - all of which require collecting documents from many client finance staff.

inferences.inference: A low-touch $99/month bookkeeping tier plus 11-50 staff implies high client volume per preparer and repetitive intake/onboarding work.
inferences.reasoning: A productised price point only works with standardised onboarding (QuickBooks setup, document collection, recurring close checklists); the site advertises QuickBooks and payroll implementation as repeatable offerings rather than bespoke projects.

inferences.inference: The firm is not answerable to AI search or to a prospective client's first question ('are you near me?').
inferences.reasoning: The title omits East Brunswick, the meta description contains template placeholder text, and the JSON-LD has no LocalBusiness/AccountingService node, no address and no phone - so no machine-readable locality, hours or service data is exposed even though the address is in the page header.

inferences.inference: The /about-rakoty/ and /non-profit/ demo pages suggest the site was built from a purchased theme and never finished, so content ownership likely sits with whoever built it rather than in-house.
inferences.reasoning: Fictitious staff names and unrelated consulting copy remain live years after the 2020 build date, and the homepage content dates to 2020 with only cosmetic page rewrites in 2026.

data_gaps: Google review count is inconsistent across mirrors: a directory quoting Google on 2026-11-08 says 16 reviews, another mirror shows 12; the limited Maps view I could load displayed only the 5.0 rating.
LinkedIn company page returned HTTP 403, so headcount, founding year and any listed officers could not be verified from the primary source.
No owner or staff roster is published on the firm's own site; no NJ Board of Accountancy / CPA firm licence was confirmed (a directory explicitly says state licence not checked).
No job postings were found on any board, and there is no careers page, so hiring signals rest on directory headcount only.
No Yelp, BBB or Birdeye listing found; review themes therefore come from the firm's own testimonials plus reviews mirrored from Google.
Office square footage, staff count and revenue are not published anywhere I could access.
Facebook page is JavaScript-rendered and could not be read without logging in, so social posting cadence is unknown.
The /non-profit-2/ page loaded in the browser as a document with a <head> but no rendered <body>; the page text I used was extracted from the served HTML rather than from rendered content.
